children: The shift in consumer dollars from goods towards services and experiences is bullish for the travel industry and more specifically online travel agents (OTAs) who are rapidly deploying artificial intelligence as an opportunity to create richer content for travelers.

“We see AI as both a new acquisition channel and a product opportunity, but execution will determine how much of the economics and consumer relationship the OTAs ultimately retain,” Morgan Stanley analyst Matthew Cost writes in a note to clients.

Since fragmented supply is more valuable in an AI-enabled environment, OTAs with the best varied supply, direct traffic, and execution track record are the most valuable. Given its portfolio of 4.7M “unique” properties, i.e., independent hotels and alternative accommodations, Booking Holdings
stands out among peers, earning an Overweight rating and $230 price target (34% upside from Tuesday’s close) from Morgan Stanley’s Cost.
“Global scale, fragmented inventory, and a single platform agentic call option leave us most constructive on the proven OTA leader,” Cost says about Booking Holdings
At the other end is Expedia
which earns an Underweight rating. Cost sees Expedia
with a similar opportunity to build a “travel-specific AI agent” but has less confidence in Expedia’s ability to execute on this initiative.

“Expedia has broad inventory and is investing across AI-enabled planning, search and personalization. However, its weaker consumer engagement and inconsistent execution track record leave us less confident that it can translate these assets into a differentiated agent as quickly as Booking.”
Cost also considers Expedia’s
high valuation as another reason for an Underweight rating as the stock trades at one of its narrowest P/E discounts to Booking in years.
“We think that spread should be wider, reinforcing our preference for Booking,” Cost says.
Lastly, Cost upgrades Airbnb

to Equal-weight from Underweight as the company’s 90% direct traffic mix—which is seen as an important competitive advantage—and improvements to its platform make double-digit room nights growth more “credible.”
However, that growth is already priced into the stock, underpinning Cost’s Equal-weight for Airbnb
“Material upside likely requires a further step-up in growth and/or margins, reinforcing our Equal-weight view,” Cost says.
Morgan Stanley’s rating changes were reflected in the share prices of all three companies Wednesday, with Booking Holdings
and Airbnb
trading higher while Expedia
slipped after a four-session winning streak.

title: Morgan Stanley sees Booking leading the OTA race over Expedia as AI transforms travel
